title: ML-based prefetch & cache-key recommendation engine + safe-config apply runbook
creator: Maya Chen
description: Design and implement an ML-backed recommendation service that synthesizes prefix hit-rate forecasts, suggests TTL bands and cache-key reshaping, and produces a staged safe-apply plan (dry-run, shadow, canary, rollback) for KV/prefix caches. The goal is to automate low-risk tuning of caching and batching configs to reduce token/lookup cost while preserving latency SLOs.
acceptance_criteria: Service generates per-prefix hit-rate forecast with provenance for >95% of active prefixes in sample workloads
Recommended TTL bands and key-shape adjustments result in simulated cost reduction >= 15% on historical traces without violating latency SLOs in the simulator
Safe-apply plan includes automated dry-run shadow replays, a canary rollout with traffic ramp and health gates, and an automatic rollback trigger that has been tested end-to-end in staging
Documentation for operators and runbook for on-call includes clear rollback steps and postmortem checklist
tasks: Data: build sampling pipeline for prefix access traces (sparse + dense cohorts)
Model: train a light-weight hit-rate forecaster (gradient-boosted or small LSTM) with explainability features
Simulator: extend existing cache simulator to accept recommended TTL bands and key transforms and emit cost/latency/cold-miss projections
Recommender API: implement endpoint returning recommended TTL, key-reshape hints, expected hit uplift, and confidence score
Runbook: author staged-apply flow (shadow -> canary -> ramp -> full) and health gates with metric thresholds
E2E test: run shadow replays on production-like traces and validate rollback behavior
Telemetry: add dashboards (per-prefix ROI, hit uplift, applied vs recommended delta) and alerting for rollback triggers
decisions: Use a hybrid approach: deterministic heuristics for high-confidence prefixes and ML forecasts for long-tail prefixes
Limit initial automatic apply to suggested TTL bands (3 discrete buckets) rather than arbitrary per-prefix values
Canary rollout will start with 1% traffic for 2 hours then 10% for 6 hours conditional on health gates
Rollbacks are automated when either 1) 99th percentile latency increases by >15% relative to baseline or 2) observed miss-rate spike >3x forecast in canary window
rollback_plan: Shadow replays run for 48h prior to any apply to detect regressions in simulated metrics
During canary, continual checksum-style compare between baseline and candidate cache behavior; on trigger, immediately flip canary traffic back to baseline and mark config as 'reverted'
Provide an operator CLI to force immediate revert for any release; include PR link and apply metadata in revert commit
Record revert reason and metrics snapshot to the change log and create an automated follow-up ticket with suggested mitigations
notes: Prior work: leverages sampling and hit-modeling foundations from ENG-314159 and the staged-apply harness in ENG-468005
We will not change cache eviction policies or shard topology in this iteration; focus scope on TTL bands and key-shape hints
Aim for runtime overhead <5% CPU for the recommender on dedicated control-plane instances
Confidence calibration: return "confidence": high|medium|low with clear provenance so Console can show a 'recommended/auto-apply' toggle
